analysis:
All changes are in the CI threat-review tooling under .github/scripts/threat_review/. None touch provider, coordinator, or attestation code, so the retained provider threat IDs (T-041, TB-011 and others) are not affected.

bedrock.py:
- It adds a native Bedrock outputConfig json_schema built via structured_output.bedrock_schema (head lines 103-104).
- It adds Sol-only additionalModelRequestFields strict mode (head 107-110).
- Fallback semantics are unchanged: only UNAVAILABLE codes trigger the OpenRouter backup (head 135-136). A ValidationException caused by the new fields would fail hard with no automatic fallback, which is an availability risk only.
- The local validator in budget_scan still checks results.

budget_runner.py:
- run() drops the `root` parameter. The threat model is now loaded with canonical_at(github, base) (head 170) instead of the checked-out docs/threat-model.yaml. This is consistent with the BASE-revision requirement and removes any reliance on the working-tree file.
- canonical_at is not supplied, so its handling of path, ref pinning and errors is unverified. Callers of run() must be updated for the removed argument; that is also not in evidence.
- lifecycle_phase is added to diagnostics. It is a fixed set of strings, with no secrets.

budget_scan.py:
- Integration prompts now include integration_source, produced by replay_source(self.source, reviewed_source_ids[model]) (head 164-169). It replays source units that the same model already reviewed.
- This adds no new data exposure beyond what source passes already send to the provider, but it increases prompt size and untrusted PR content in integration, which is a prompt-injection surface that already existed. The prompt text still labels analyses and source as untrusted.
- The cache identity digests the whole message, so it includes the replayed source. The identity also covers INSTRUCTIONS and the reviewed ids, so cache poisoning across different replays is not evident.
- integration_context.replay_source is not supplied. Its size cap, omitted-unit accounting and the 180k Bedrock request bound (bedrock.py head 111) are unverified. An oversize request would raise BudgetStopped, which is an availability effect only.

No concrete security regression is established.
